title: Grid 2
explanation: The grid has 1e10 cells, but only 3000 walls. Sort walls; dp[i] = paths to wall i that touch no earlier wall = all paths minus those through an earlier first wall.
traps: Precompute factorials up to H + W for C(a + b, a) mod p.

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[i] = number of paths from the start to wall i (in sorted order) that hit no other wall before it
dp[i] = number of paths through wall i
options.why: Paths through several walls get counted multiple times.

options.text: dp[mask] = paths avoiding the walls in mask

extraLayers.explanation: When the grid is huge but special points are few, make the special points the states and count free paths between them with binomials.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: dp[i] = C(r_i + c_i − 2, r_i − 1) − Σ over walls j before i (r_j ≤ r_i, c_j ≤ c_i) of dp[j] · C(r_i − r_j + c_i − c_j, r_i − r_j); treat the target as wall N+1
dp[i] = C(r_i + c_i − 2, r_i − 1) − Σ C(paths through j)
options.why: Subtracts paths through every earlier wall, double-subtracting paths that hit several.
Each wall blocks many paths, not one.

extraLayers.explanation: Classify bad paths by the first wall they hit — each bad path is subtracted exactly once.
